description: We are Team Shawerma. Like the perfect shawerma, our solution is layered, wrapped with precision, and made to satisfy real-world hunger. We turn NASA's open data into something everyone can digest. From Lebanon, with love & extra toum.
summary: Captain Leo’s Space Adventure turns NASA data into a story kids can play. It starts with the Sun and its eight planets, then travels to Mars. There, players tap Spirit and Opportunity to hear their true missions: where they landed, how far they drove, and what they found. Finally, they explore an ancient lake bed and collect 3 water clues from Gusev Crater, Meridiani Planum, and the rock record. The goal is to make children feel like real explorers and understand that robots are our eyes and hands in space.
details:
Captain Leo’s Space Adventure is an interactive 3D website for kids. It has 5 chapters: 1) Our Solar System, 2) Take My Hand, 3) Welcome to Mars, 4) Twin Explorers, 5) The Ancient Lake. The player starts with Captain Leo, flies past the Sun and the eight planets, holds Leo’s hand to warp to Mars, then taps Spirit and Opportunity to hear their true stories in cards. Finally, they travel to an ancient lake bed and tap 3 glowing orbs to collect water clues. A Fact Book, progress bar, HUD, and a final “Junior Mars Explorer” badge guide the whole journey.What benefits does it have?

It turns hard NASA science into a story kids can play, not just read. Kids learn real facts while playing: where Spirit and Opportunity landed, how far they drove, and why their discoveries matter. The voice + text + lip-sync helps young readers and English learners follow along.What is the intended impact?

To make children feel like real explorers and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts. We want kids in Lebanon and everywhere to believe space is for them, and to understand that robots are our eyes, hands, and feet in space.What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We built it with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript using Three.js (r128) for 3D, WebGL, and Canvas textures for planets, Mars terrain, and characters. Voices are pre-recorded MP3 files synced to on-screen text and lip movement. It is hosted on Netlify and is optimized for laptop / desktop browsers. No install or special hardware is needed.How is your project creative?

Instead of a slideshow, we made a playable space journey with a friendly astronaut guide, waving, hopping in Mars gravity, and talking with real voice. The rovers have faces, eyes, and smiles, they drive, idle, and hop. The ancient lake slowly appears as you find clues, so discovery feels real.What factors did your team consider?

We designed this project for laptop / desktop, because the 3D Solar System, the Mars terrain, and the dialogue need a wide screen. On a phone the screen becomes narrow and the experience is tight, so we recommend playing on a laptop for the best view. We designed for kids aged 6-12: big buttons, simple English, short sentences, bright colors, and a Sound On/Off button. We considered accessibility: every voice line also shows as text, and we added reduced-motion support. We used only real NASA facts: Spirit landed Jan 3, 2004 in Gusev Crater and drove 4.8 miles, Opportunity landed Jan 24, 2004 at Meridiani Planum and drove 28.06 miles. We also kept the project fully original and browser-based so any school can open it with one link.
